rv.q: It isn’t groundbreaking but it all makes for a lovely afternoon.
It is more of an aesthetic triumph than a fully blown celebration of panto spirit, then.
Director Robin Belfield has done a wonderful job of following panto tradition, staging the show with moments of brilliant slapstick and mild audience interaction.

Ashh Blackwood is endlessly upbeat as Buttons, while Chrissy Bhima offers a likeably quirky Cinderella. Colin Burnicle brings classic cheesy comedy as ugly sister Muruduth, and his Geordie Fairy Kween is an earthy delight. Lauren Redding shines in both her roles of ugly sister Mikayla and Dandini, while Durone Stokes is suitably campy as Prince M.

cn.t: Critics find this Cinderella serviceable but uneven, with scene-stealing supporting performances brightening an otherwise safe retelling that doesn't fully deliver the magic it promises.
